- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

r03.

The premise is incorrect: **there is no nightly database-cleanup job registered in this repository's cron scheduler.** No time can be reported because no such job exists.

What's actually there:

- `internal/scheduler/` is a self-contained, general-purpose cron scheduler library (`scheduler.go`, `job.go`, `parser.go`, `middleware.go`). It is **not wired into the application at all** — the only files importing `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/scheduler` are its own tests (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go:10` and `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:13`). Nothing under `cmd/`, `server/`, or `store/` registers any job with it.

- The `0 2 * * *` (2 AM daily) cleanup schedule you may be thinking of appears only in **documentation and example code**, never as a live registration:
  - `internal/scheduler/doc.go:15-16` — package doc example, `Name: "daily-cleanup"`, `Schedule: "0 2 * * *"`
  - `internal/scheduler/example_test.go:97-99` — `Example_multipleJobs`, `Name: "cleanup"`, `Schedule: "0 2 * * *"`
  - `internal/scheduler/README.md:34-37` and `:241-245` — illustrative snippets (`daily-cleanup`, `stale-session-cleanup`)

The actual background work in the server is not cron-scheduled and not database cleanup:

- `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27,30` — a ticker-based runner refreshing S3 presigned links every 12 hours (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`), started at `server/server.go:162-169`.
- `store/cache/cache.go:46-47,199-218` — an in-memory cache eviction loop running every 5 minutes, unrelated to the database.
- `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` — a one-shot payload rebuild, no schedule.
